name.text: Selecting livestock for market and choosing crops for a shamba

questiontext.text:
(a) A farmer in Kakamega has \({@pn1@}\) goats and wants to take \({@pr1@}\) of them to the market to sell. In how many ways can the farmer choose which goats to take?

Number of ways = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) A family has \({@pn2@}\) different crops they could plant (such as maize, beans, sukuma wiki, tomatoes and onions) but have room in their shamba for only \({@pr2@}\) different crops. How many different groups of crops can they choose?

Number of groups = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Because the order in which items are chosen does not create a different selection, use the combination formula:

\(\displaystyle {}_nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}\)

Part (a): Choosing \({@pr1@}\) goats out of \({@pn1@}\) to take to the market
Choosing which \({@pr1@}\) goats to sell is the same as choosing which \({@pn1@} - {@pr1@} = {@rem1@}\) goats to leave behind, so \({}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@rem1@}}\). Substitute \(n = {@pn1@}\) and \(r = {@pr1@}\), expand \({@pn1@}!\) down to \({@pr1@}!\), and cancel \({@pr1@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn1@}}C_{{@pr1@}} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,({@pn1@} - {@pr1@})!} = \frac{{@pn1@}!}{{@pr1@}!\,{@rem1@}!} = \frac{{@num1_factors@} \times {@pr1@}!}{{@pr1@}! \times ({@den1_factors@})} = \frac{{@num1_factors@}}{{@den1_factors@}} = \frac{{@num1_prod@}}{{@den1_prod@}} = {@ta1@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of ways} = {@ta1@} }\)

Part (b): Choosing \({@pr2@}\) crops out of \({@pn2@}\) for the shamba
Planting maize and beans is the same group as planting beans and maize, so order does not matter. Substitute \(n = {@pn2@}\) and \(r = {@pr2@}\), simplify \(({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})! = {@rem2@}!\), and cancel \({@rem2@}!\):

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})!} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@} \times {@rem2@}!}{({@den2_factors@}) \times {@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@num2_factors@}}{{@den2_factors@}} = \frac{{@num2_prod@}}{{@den2_prod@}} = {@ta2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of groups} = {@ta2@} }\)
